newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief Annan sends new envoy to Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: UN chief Annan sends new envoy to Afghanistan.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Tuesday appointed Algerian diplomat Lakhdar Brahimi to go to Afghanistan and report back to him on the country's seemingly intractable civil war.

Brahimi, U.N. officials said, would not replace the current special U.N. envoy, Norbert Hull of Germany, but bring back a fresh perspective on the direction of international peace efforts in the country.

U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said Brahimi would leave soon to "undertake a short-term mission in order to assess the U.N. peacemaking activities in Afghanistan" and submit his findings in time for the 52nd session of the U.N. General Assembly in September.
Brahimi, a former Algerian foreign minister, headed the U.N. operation in Haiti from September 1994 until March 1996.

Annan has said that the warring Afghan parties seemed bent on resolving their problems through military means and had paid no at attention to the many calls for a ceasefire and dialogue made by the Security Council, Holl and many others.
The fundamentalist Islamic Taliban movement, which captured Kabul, the capital, last September, controls more than two-thirds of the country and is battling an opposition alliance.
The conflict is increasingly being fuelled by strong ethnic feelings between the predominantly Pushtun Taliban and the Tajiks, Hazaras and Uzbeks who comprise the opposition camp.
